sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच
संन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ।
तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते।।
image_english: Renunciation and devotional work both lead to liberation, but devotional service is better.
caption:
Chapter 5, Verse 2

Kṛṣṇa clarifies the goal. ‘sannyāsaḥ karma-yogaś ca’ (The renunciation of work and work in devotion) are both good for liberation (‘niḥśreyasa-karāv ubhau’). ‘tayos tu karma-sannyāsāt’ (But of the two, work in devotional service) is better than ‘renunciation of work’ (‘karma-yogo viśiṣyate’). Why? Because renunciation without devotion is dry, difficult, and risky. It is hard to simply ‘stop’ desiring. But Karma-yoga (engaging the senses in service) is easier, safer, and more natural for the embodied soul. It is better to use the hands for God than to tie them behind your back.
